title: Open-immersion and etale extension by zero have the same adjunction
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion], which is etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and let $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be the category of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $T=U,X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $j_!$ be the extension by zero of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], the sheafification of the presheaf $j_{p!}F$, with the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] (unit $\eta_j$, counit $\varepsilon_j$), where $j^{-1}$ is the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Let $j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ be the extension $v_!$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] for $v=j$, the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{s\in\Hom_X(V,U)}F(V,s)$, with the adjunction $j^{\mathrm{et}}_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] (unit $\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_j$, counit $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_j$), the adjunction used in [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]. For $F\in\Mod(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $V\in X_{\Et}$ let $\iota_{F,V}:(j_{p!}F)(V)\to\bigoplus_{s\in\Hom_X(V,U)}F(V,s)$ be the inclusion of $F(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)$ as the unique summand when $V$ factors through $U$ by $\varphi$, and the zero map of zero modules otherwise, and let $\kappa_F:j_!F\to j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $\iota_F$. Then $\kappa$ is a natural isomorphism $j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ of functors $\Mod(U_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and it identifies the two adjunctions: for $F\in\Mod(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $G\in\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $\alpha:F\to j^{-1}G$, the transpose of $\alpha$ under the adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] is the transpose of $\alpha$ under the adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] composed with $\kappa_F$. Equivalently $\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F}=j^{-1}(\kappa_F)\circ\eta_{j,F}$ and $\varepsilon_{j,G}=\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,G}\circ\kappa_{j^{-1}G}$.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), statement and proof: the hom bijection alpha -> alpha' through the presheaf V -> sum over Mor(V,U); with etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03S3 (definition-extension-zero) and the following paragraph (j_! is the sheafification of j_{p!}, characterized by the functorial Hom isomorphism)

proof.text: Write $P_F=j_{p!}F$ and $Q_F(V)=\bigoplus_{s\in\Hom_X(V,U)}F(V,s)$. The objects-over-$U$ clause of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] says that this index set is empty or a singleton, and any lift $s$ makes $(V,s)$ an object of $U_{\Et}$. If it is a singleton, define $\rho_{F,V}:Q_F(V)\to P_F(V)$ by sending the unique summand identically to $F(V,s)$; if it is empty, both modules are zero and use their unique map. Then $\rho_{F,V}\iota_{F,V}=1$ and $\iota_{F,V}\rho_{F,V}=1$, by evaluation on the unique summand, or on zero. For $a:V'\to V$, when $V$ has a lift, the summand restriction of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] sends it to the unique lift $sa$ and applies $F(a)$, exactly as $P_F$ does. When $V$ has no lift, both restrictions have zero source, even if $V'$ has a lift. Thus $\iota_F$ and $\rho_F$ are inverse presheaf maps. A morphism $F\to F'$ acts by its component on each summand, so these maps also commute with every such morphism.

source.place: Tag 03DI (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero), direct-sum presheaf and the construction alpha -> alpha′ in its proof; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03S3 (etale-cohomology-definition-extension-zero), following paragraph and equation-j-p-shriek

proof.text: Let $q^P_F:P_F\to j_!F$ and $q^Q_F:Q_F\to j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F$ be the sheafification maps. By [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], $q^Q_F\iota_F$ induces the unique map $\kappa_F:j_!F\to j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F$ with $\kappa_Fq^P_F=q^Q_F\iota_F$. Likewise $q^P_F\rho_F$ induces $\lambda_F:j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F\to j_!F$. Precomposing $\lambda_F\kappa_F$ with $q^P_F$ gives $q^P_F\rho_F\iota_F=q^P_F$, so uniqueness in sheafification gives $\lambda_F\kappa_F=1$. The other identity follows after precomposition with $q^Q_F$. Naturality in $F$ follows by precomposing its required square with $q^P_F$, using Step 1 and uniqueness. Hence the specified sheafification $\kappa$ is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 03DI (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero), direct-sum presheaf and the construction alpha -> alpha′ in its proof; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03S3 (etale-cohomology-definition-extension-zero), following paragraph and equation-j-p-shriek

proof.text: We compute the sum construction's Hom bijection, rather than infer its value from the existence of a left adjoint. For a presheaf map $t:Q_F\to G$, restrict $t_V$ to the summand indexed by $s:V\to U$ to obtain $\alpha_{(V,s)}:F(V,s)\to G(V)$. Here $G(V)=j^{-1}G(V,s)$, the restriction identification stated in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Naturality of $t$ and the summand restriction formula of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] give $G(a)\alpha_{(V,s)}=\alpha_{(V',sa)}F(a)$ for every $a:(V',sa)\to(V,s)$; thus these components define $\alpha:F\to j^{-1}G$. Conversely such an $\alpha$ defines $t_{\alpha,V}$ by $t_{\alpha,V}(\operatorname{in}_s x)=\alpha_{(V,s)}(x)$, extended $\Lambda$-linearly; for an empty index set it is the zero map. The same displayed equality proves naturality. The two constructions are inverse since they agree on each summand; they commute with precomposition in $F$ and postcomposition in $G$ component by component.

source.place: Tag 03DI (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero), direct-sum presheaf and the construction alpha -> alpha′ in its proof; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03S3 (etale-cohomology-definition-extension-zero), following paragraph and equation-j-p-shriek

proof.text: Sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] identifies maps $j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F\to G$ with presheaf maps $Q_F\to G$ by precomposition with $q^Q_F$. Compose this bijection with Step 3. It is natural in $F,G$, hence is an adjunction Hom bijection by [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]. This is precisely the canonical adjunction $j^{\mathrm{et}}_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives]: we have written out the direct-sum/sheafification construction of Stacks 03DI that defines that adjunction, including its inverse check. In particular the transpose $T_{\mathrm{et}}(\alpha)$ is characterized by $T_{\mathrm{et}}(\alpha)q^Q_F=t_\alpha$. This calculation uses the cited injective-restriction node for its adjunction assertion only; it does not assume its statement contains the transpose formula.

source.place: Tag 03DI (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero), direct-sum presheaf and the construction alpha -> alpha′ in its proof; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03S3 (etale-cohomology-definition-extension-zero), following paragraph and equation-j-p-shriek

proof.text: For $\alpha:F\to j^{-1}G$, [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] says its open-extension transpose $T_{\mathrm{op}}(\alpha)$ is induced by $p_{\alpha,V}:P_F(V)\to G(V)$, equal to $\alpha_{(V,s)}$ if a lift exists and the zero map otherwise. At each $V$, Step 3 gives $t_{\alpha,V}\iota_{F,V}=p_{\alpha,V}$ on the unique summand, or on the zero source. Therefore $T_{\mathrm{et}}(\alpha)\kappa_Fq^P_F=T_{\mathrm{et}}(\alpha)q^Q_F\iota_F=t_\alpha\iota_F=p_\alpha=T_{\mathrm{op}}(\alpha)q^P_F$. Uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] gives $T_{\mathrm{op}}(\alpha)=T_{\mathrm{et}}(\alpha)\kappa_F$, proving the required equality of transposes for every $F,G,\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 03DI (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero), direct-sum presheaf and the construction alpha -> alpha′ in its proof; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 03S3 (etale-cohomology-definition-extension-zero), following paragraph and equation-j-p-shriek

proof.text: For completeness let $\Phi_{\mathrm{op}},\Phi_{\mathrm{et}}$ denote the forward Hom bijections. Step 5 gives $\Phi_{\mathrm{op}}(b\kappa_F)=\Phi_{\mathrm{et}}(b)$ for every $b:j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F\to G$. Take $G=j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F$ and $b=1$. The formula $\Phi(a)=j^{-1}(a)\eta_F$ and $\Phi(1)=\eta_F$ in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] yield $j^{-1}(\kappa_F)\eta_{j,F}=\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F}$. Next take $F=j^{-1}G$ and $\alpha=1$ in Step 5. Since the transpose of $1_{j^{-1}G}$ is the counit by the same cited node, $\varepsilon_{j,G}=\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,G}\kappa_{j^{-1}G}$. These are the asserted unit and counit identities.

Sources checked: Stacks 03DI (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero), including the summandwise construction alpha -> alpha' in its proof; Stacks 03S3 and equation-j-p-shriek; the main-20261015 proof of cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change ('degreewise isomorphisms'); and the blueprint proof of lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives. The cited statements give what each step takes from them. Step 1: the comparison iota/rho between the single-lift presheaf and the sum presheaf is correct, including a restriction from a V with no lift to a V' with a lift. Step 2: kappa and its inverse come from the universal property of sheafification only. Step 3: the presheaf Hom bijection is correct, and its naturality is exactly naturality on the morphisms of U_et. Step 4: the statement of lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives only says an adjunction exists, so 'its adjunction' has to mean the canonical one. That canonical construction (Stacks 03DI proof, the node's blueprint proof) is exactly what Steps 3-4 write out. Both adjunctions use the same j^{-1} and the same identification j^{-1}G(V,s)=G(V). I accept this reading, and the step says openly that the cited statement does not contain the transpose formula. Step 5 proves the transposes are equal (T_op = T_et kappa) through the universal property, not by abstract uniqueness of adjoints. Step 6 gets both unit and counit identities with the right domains and composition order. Edge cases checked: j = id, U empty, X empty, Lambda = 0, F = 0. The coefficients are an arbitrary commutative Lambda. There is no SGA, no cycle and no duplicate: a grep of the nodes citing the extension-by-zero and restriction-injectives nodes found none stating this comparison. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. No tool_uses, no changes.

lean.statement: theorem openImmersionToEtaleLowerShriek_adjunction_agreement (Λ : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing Λ] {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] : IsIso (openImmersionToEtaleLowerShriek Λ j) ∧ (∀ (F : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)) (α : F ⟶ (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).obj G), ((openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).homEquiv F G).symm α = (openImmersionToEtaleLowerShriek Λ j).app F ≫ ((etaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j inferInstance).homEquiv F G).symm α) ∧ (∀ (F : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)), (etaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j inferInstance).unit.app F = (openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).unit.app F ≫ (upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).map ((openImmersionToEtaleLowerShriek Λ j).app F)) ∧ (∀ (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ)), (openImmersionLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).counit.app G = (openImmersionToEtaleLowerShriek Λ j).app ((upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j).obj G) ≫ (etaleLowerShriekUpperStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ) j inferInstance).counit.app G)
